examples.question: The Story of the Piano An original passage written for LearnAce 1 About three hundred years ago in Italy, an instrument maker named Bartolomeo Cristofori built a new keyboard instrument. Earlier keyboards, like the harpsichord, plucked their strings, so every note sounded equally loud. 2 Cristofori's instrument used small hammers to strike the strings. When a player pressed a key gently, the note was soft. When the player pressed hard, the note was loud. He named it the "gravicembalo col piano e forte" — the "harpsichord with soft and loud." Over time, people shortened the name to piano. How was Cristofori's instrument different?
examples.answer: Hammers struck the strings, so notes could be soft or loud
choices: Hammers struck the strings, so notes could be soft or loud

examples.question: The Inuksuk An original passage written for LearnAce 1 Across the Arctic stand stone figures called inuksuit (the singular is inuksuk). The word comes from Inuktitut and means "to act in the capacity of a human." For thousands of years, Inuit have built these stone structures for many purposes. 2 Some inuksuit mark a good place to fish or hunt. Others point the way home across the open tundra, where there are few trees or landmarks. Certain arrangements warned travellers of danger, such as thin ice. A few are sacred and are treated with great respect. 3 Building an inuksuk takes skill. Stones must be balanced carefully so the structure can stand for generations in fierce Arctic winds. 4 Today the inuksuk is a symbol of Canada and appears on the flag of Nunavut. For many people it represents leadership, cooperation and the importance of helping others find their way. Which purpose is NOT mentioned in the passage?
examples.answer: Marking the border between two countries
choices: Marking the border between two countries

subject: english
title: Read about history

examples.question: The Underground Railroad An original passage written for LearnAce 1 The Underground Railroad was not a real railroad. It was a secret network of people and safe houses that helped enslaved people in the United States escape to freedom in the 1800s. 2 People who guided escapees were called "conductors," and the safe houses were called "stations." Travelling mostly at night, freedom seekers followed the North Star. Many journeyed all the way to Canada, where slavery had been abolished. 3 Harriet Tubman, who escaped slavery herself, became one of the most famous conductors. She returned again and again to lead others to safety. Why did freedom seekers often travel to Canada?
choices: It was closer than any other place

examples.question: The Building of the Canadian Pacific Railway An original passage written for LearnAce 1 When British Columbia joined Canada in 1871, it was promised a railway connecting it to the rest of the country. Building it was an enormous challenge. 2 Workers had to cut through the rocky Canadian Shield and blast tunnels through the Rocky Mountains. Thousands of Chinese labourers did some of the most dangerous work, often for lower pay than other workers, and many lost their lives. 3 On November 7, 1885, the "last spike" was hammered in at Craigellachie, B.C. The railway linked Canada from the Atlantic to the Pacific and helped the young country grow. Which group did some of the most dangerous work?
